$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. LoopValidationReport per loop-validation-rules.v1.json's own top-level description: 'A validation report MUST include this rulesetVersion, the semantic digest of the definition being validated, the surface implementation identity, and findings sorted deterministically (by namespace, then code, then nodeId/edgeId).' `findings[].code` MUST be a code from that frozen registry — this schema cross-references it (pattern + duplicated namespace enum) rather than re-enumerating all 24 current rules, so an additive registry minor bump never forces a schema change (matching loop-package-manifest.schema.json's CapabilityRequest precedent).
title: LoopValidationReport
description: The output of the CONTAINER_VERIFIED-to-PARSED_VALIDATED transition (LOOP_IMPORT_ACTIVATION_CONTRACT.md §3): schema/graph/engine-policy validation against loop-validation-rules.v1.json, run before anything is created or changed. Also produced independently at build time (LOOP_ENGINEERING_SPEC_V2.1 §20's build pipeline step 2, VALIDATE_SEMANTIC_GRAPH) and re-run whenever a definition changes.

schemaVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH of this report's shape. A reader MUST reject an unrecognized MAJOR (FB-RAT-COM-003).

reportId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this report (FB-RAT-COM-002).

rulesetVersion.description: loop-validation-rules.v1.json's own `rulesetVersion` value, cross-referenced not redefined — pinned as the sole valid value while that registry stays at its current frozen major (a future registry MAJOR bump is a new `rulesetVersion` string, and a new const here, not a relaxed pattern).

semanticDigest.description: The definition.json being validated, digested per semantic-digest.v1.json's chosen 'sha256:<hex>' serialization — NOT floop-container-format.v1.json's packageContentDigest (a different, wider digest over the whole semantic file set).

semanticDigestVersion.description: semantic-digest.v1.json's own `semanticDigestVersion` value, paired with `semanticDigest` above (mirrors LoopBuildReceipt's identical pairing in contracts/kotlin/LoopPackageContracts.kt).

surfaceImplementation.description: Which validator produced this report — phone or browser, and its own build identity (LOOP_DUAL_SURFACE_ARCHITECTURE.md: both surfaces MUST independently validate; a report is only ever trusted as evidence of ITS OWN surface's validation pass, never assumed to also speak for the other surface).

findings.description: MUST be sorted deterministically by (namespace, then code, then nodeId/edgeId) per loop-validation-rules.v1.json's own top-level description. This is a documented ordering invariant, not one JSON Schema's array-validation vocabulary can express structurally (there is no native 'items sorted by these fields' keyword) — see fixtures/loops/loop-validation-report/adversarial for the schema-valid-but-unsorted case.

highestSeverity.description: Convenience rollup: the most severe value across `findings[].severity` (ERROR > WARNING > INFO), or null when `findings` is empty. Not independently authoritative — a consumer MUST NOT trust this field over recomputing it from `findings` when the two disagree; see the `allOf` below for the one direction this schema DOES check structurally.

createdAtUtc.description: UTC instant this report was produced (FB-RAT-COM-004).

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

surface.description: LOOP_DUAL_SURFACE_ARCHITECTURE.md's two surfaces — which one ran this validation pass.

ValidationNamespace.description: loop-validation-rules.v1.json's `namespaces[].prefix` list, duplicated verbatim. A finding's `namespace` field exists (rather than requiring every reader to re-parse it out of `code`) specifically so the required sort key (namespace, then code, then nodeId/edgeId) has a field to sort on without string-parsing `code` at read time.

namespace.description: MUST equal the LOOP-<NAMESPACE> segment of `code` (i.e. `code` with its trailing '-NNN' suffix removed) — this schema does not cross-check the two structurally beyond both being independently valid (namespace against the closed enum above, code against the pattern below), because a strict cross-field regex-equality check is not expressible in portable draft 2020-12 without duplicating the full 10-way namespace branch as another `if`/`then` chain; see fixtures/loops/loop-validation-report/adversarial for the schema-valid-but-mismatched case.

code.description: A rule code from loop-validation-rules.v1.json (e.g. 'LOOP-PKG-006'). This schema checks shape only; membership in the frozen registry is validated by the rule engine, not here — an additive registry minor bump never requires a schema change.

severity.description: loop-validation-rules.v1.json's `severityLevels`, verbatim. The registry's OWN severity for a given code is authoritative — a producer MUST NOT emit a severity other than the one that code's registry entry declares; this schema cannot check that cross-reference structurally.

objectType.description: e.g. 'node', 'edge', 'definition', 'file', 'bindingProfile' — matches the rule's own `objectType` field in loop-validation-rules.v1.json.

message.description: The rule's `messageTemplate` with placeholders resolved against this specific finding's location/values.

remediation.description: Copy of the rule's own `remediation` text, or a finding-specific refinement of it.

nonDismissible.description: Copy of the rule's own `nonDismissible` flag when present (currently only LOOP-PKG-006, invisible/control Unicode) — a UI MUST NOT offer a dismiss action for a finding carrying this as true, regardless of severity.
